subskill: supplementary angles
prompt: Two angles are supplementary. One of the angles measures 47°. What is the measure, in degrees, of the other angle?
explanation: Supplementary angles have measures that add to 180°, so the other angle measures 180 - 47 = 133 degrees. "43" is 90 - 47, the measure of the COMPLEMENT of the given angle. "94" doubles the given angle, 2 x 47. "47" repeats the given angle, which would be right for a pair of congruent vertical angles but not for a supplementary pair.

subskill: circumference of a circle from its radius
prompt: A circle has a radius of 7 centimeters. Using 22/7 for π, what is the circumference of the circle, in centimeters?
explanation: The circumference is 2πr = 2 x (22/7) x 7 = 44 centimeters. "14" is the diameter, 2 x 7, one step short of the circumference. "22" is πr, which leaves out the factor of 2. "88" comes from putting the diameter 14 into 2πr, 2 x (22/7) x 14, so the radius is doubled twice.

subskill: the third angle of a triangle
prompt: Two of the angles of a triangle measure 52° and 61°. What is the measure, in degrees, of the third angle?
explanation: The three angles of a triangle add to 180°, so the third angle measures 180 - 52 - 61 = 67 degrees. "113" is 52 + 61, the sum of the two given angles rather than what is left of 180°. "119" is 180 - 61, which uses only one of the two given angles. "29" is 180 - 90 - 61, from assuming the triangle has a right angle and discarding the 52°.

subskill: volume of a rectangular prism
prompt: A rectangular box is 6 inches long, 4 inches wide, and 5 inches high. What is the volume of the box, in cubic inches?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular box is the product of its three dimensions, 6 x 4 x 5 = 120 cubic inches. "148" is the surface area, 2(6x4 + 4x5 + 6x5). "74" is that same face sum without the doubling, 6x4 + 4x5 + 6x5. "40" applies the one-third that belongs to a pyramid, (1/3) x 6 x 4 x 5.

subskill: a leg of a right triangle from the hypotenuse and the other leg
prompt: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is 26 centimeters long and one of the legs is 10 centimeters long. How many centimeters long is the other leg?
explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem the other leg is the square root of 26^2 - 10^2 = 676 - 100 = 576, so it is 24 centimeters. "16" subtracts the lengths themselves, 26 - 10, instead of their squares. "13" halves the hypotenuse, which would be the short leg only if the triangle were a 30-60-90 triangle. "20.8" assumes a 3-4-5 triangle scaled to this hypotenuse and takes the longer leg, 26 x (4/5).

subskill: area of a parallelogram given a slant side
prompt: The figure below shows parallelogram PQRS, with the height drawn from vertex S perpendicular to side PQ. All lengths are in centimeters. What is the area of PQRS, in square centimeters?

graphic.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 350 250" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#12151C"><polygon points="40,200 250,200 300,110 90,110" fill="none" stroke="#2B3A8C" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="90" y1="110" x2="90" y2="200" stroke="#0A5C48" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5,4"/><polyline points="90,188 102,188 102,200" fill="none" stroke="#0A5C48" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="30" y="216">P</text><text x="250" y="216">Q</text><text x="304" y="106">R</text><text x="76" y="104">S</text><text x="141" y="219">14</text><text x="72" y="160">6</text><text x="44" y="152">8</text><text x="16" y="240" font-size="11" fill="#5A6474">Figure not drawn to scale.</text></svg>
graphic.caption: Figure not drawn to scale.

explanation: The area of a parallelogram is base x height, and the height is the perpendicular segment, 6, not the slant side. The area is 14 x 6 = 84 square centimeters. "112" multiplies the base by the slant side, 14 x 8. "48" multiplies the slant side by the height, 8 x 6. "44" is the perimeter, 2(14 + 8), not an area at all.

subskill: consecutive angles of a parallelogram
prompt: In parallelogram JKLM, the measure of angle J is 63°. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle K?
explanation: In a parallelogram the vertices are named in order, so angles J and K are consecutive and their measures add to 180°: angle K measures 180 - 63 = 117 degrees. "63" would be right for angle L, the angle OPPOSITE angle J, not for the one next to it. "27" treats the two angles as complementary, 90 - 63. "90" assumes the parallelogram is a rectangle, which the problem never says.

subskill: surface area of a rectangular prism
prompt: A closed rectangular box is 8 inches long, 3 inches wide, and 2 inches high. What is the total surface area of the box, in square inches?
explanation: A closed box has three pairs of congruent faces, so its surface area is 2(8x3 + 3x2 + 8x2) = 2(24 + 6 + 16) = 92 square inches. "46" is 24 + 6 + 16, one face of each pair, so it is half the surface area. "48" is the volume, 8 x 3 x 2. "52" is the total edge length, 4(8 + 3 + 2).

subskill: side length of a square from its area
prompt: A square has an area of 50 square inches. What is the length of one side of the square, in inches, to the nearest tenth?
explanation: The side of a square is the square root of its area, and the square root of 50 is 7.071..., which is 7.1 inches to the nearest tenth. "10" is the DIAGONAL of this square, the square root of 2 x 50. "12.5" divides the area by the four sides, 50/4, which is not how area relates to side length. "25" halves the area, 50/2.

subskill: the side opposite the 30 degree angle in a 30-60-90 triangle
prompt: In a right triangle, one of the acute angles measures 30° and the hypotenuse is 18 centimeters long. How many centimeters long is the side opposite the 30° angle?
explanation: In a 30-60-90 triangle the side opposite the 30° angle is half the hypotenuse, so it is 18/2 = 9 centimeters. "15.6" is the OTHER leg, the one opposite the 60° angle, 18 x (square root of 3)/2. "10.4" divides the hypotenuse by the square root of 3 instead of by 2. "6" divides by 3 because of the 30 in the angle measure.

subskill: an inscribed angle and the central angle on the same arc
prompt: In the circle below, point O is the centre and points A, B, and C lie on the circle. What is the measure, in degrees, of central angle BOC?

graphic.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 350 250" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#12151C"><circle cx="175" cy="125" r="88" fill="none" stroke="#2B3A8C" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="88" y1="110" x2="198" y2="40" stroke="#0A5C48" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="88" y1="110" x2="251" y2="81" stroke="#0A5C48" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="175" y1="125" x2="198" y2="40" stroke="#8A3B12" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="175" y1="125" x2="251" y2="81" stroke="#8A3B12" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="175" cy="125" r="3.2" fill="#12151C"/><path d="M122,89 A40,40 0 0 1 127,103" fill="none" stroke="#0A5C48" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="70" y="116">A</text><text x="202" y="34">B</text><text x="256" y="80">C</text><text x="168" y="144">O</text><text x="149" y="86">34°</text><text x="16" y="240" font-size="11" fill="#5A6474">Figure not drawn to scale.</text></svg>
graphic.caption: Figure not drawn to scale.

explanation: Angle BAC is inscribed in the circle and angle BOC is the central angle on the same arc BC, so the central angle is twice the inscribed one: 2 x 34 = 68 degrees. "34" assumes the two angles are equal. "17" halves the inscribed angle instead of doubling it, reversing the relationship. "56" is 90 - 34, the complement of the marked angle.

subskill: area of a regular hexagon from its side length
prompt: A regular hexagon has sides 6 inches long. What is the area of the hexagon, in square inches, to the nearest tenth?
explanation: A regular hexagon splits into six equilateral triangles of side 6, each of area (square root of 3)/4 x 6^2 = 15.588..., so the hexagon covers 6 x 15.588... = 93.5 square inches to the nearest tenth. "15.6" is one of those six triangles, the value one step before the final multiplication. "36" is 6 x 6, the perimeter of the hexagon. "108" uses (1/2) x 6 x 6 for each triangle, taking the side itself as the height.

subskill: volume of a pyramid
prompt: A pyramid has a square base with sides 9 meters long and a height of 10 meters. What is the volume of the pyramid, in cubic meters?
explanation: The volume of a pyramid is one third of the base area times the height: (1/3) x 9^2 x 10 = 270 cubic meters. "810" leaves out the one third, which is the volume of a PRISM on the same base. "405" uses one half rather than one third. "243" uses the base edge 9 as the height, (1/3) x 81 x 9.

subskill: indirect measurement with similar triangles
prompt: At the same time of day, a student 5 feet tall casts a shadow 4 feet long and a nearby flagpole casts a shadow 26 feet long. How many feet tall is the flagpole?
explanation: The student and the flagpole make similar right triangles, so height/shadow is the same for both: the flagpole is 5 x 26/4 = 32.5 feet tall. "20.8" inverts the ratio, 4 x 26/5, using shadow/height. "130" is 5 x 26 with the division by 4 left out. "35" adds the three given lengths, 5 + 26 + 4, treating a proportion as a sum.

subskill: reflection across the line y = x
prompt: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, the point (−3, 8) is reflected across the line y = x. What is the x-coordinate of the image point?
explanation: Reflecting across the line y = x exchanges the two coordinates, so (−3, 8) maps to (8, −3) and the image has x-coordinate 8. "3" is the x-coordinate after a reflection across the y-axis, which negates x instead of swapping. "-3" leaves the x-coordinate alone, which is what a reflection across the x-axis does. "-8" is the x-coordinate after a reflection across the line y = −x, which swaps AND negates.

subskill: an acute angle from the tangent ratio
prompt: A loading ramp rises 3.5 feet over a horizontal run of 12 feet. To the nearest degree, what angle does the ramp make with the horizontal ground?
explanation: The rise is opposite the angle and the run is adjacent to it, so the tangent of the angle is 3.5/12 and the angle is 16 degrees to the nearest degree. "17" uses the inverse sine of 3.5/12, which would be right only if 12 were the ramp itself rather than the horizontal run. "73" uses the inverse cosine of 3.5/12. "74" is the inverse tangent of 12/3.5, the OTHER acute angle of the triangle, the one the ramp makes with the vertical.

subskill: area of the region between two concentric circles
prompt: A circular running track has an outer radius of 30 meters and an inner radius of 24 meters. Using 3.14 for π, what is the area of the track surface, the region between the two circles, in square meters?
explanation: The region between the circles is the outer disc minus the inner disc: 3.14(30^2 - 24^2) = 3.14(900 - 576) = 1017.36 square meters. "2826" is the outer disc alone, 3.14 x 900, with nothing removed. "1808.64" is the inner disc alone, 3.14 x 576, the part that is NOT track. "4634.64" adds the two areas instead of subtracting them.

subskill: the position of the hour hand on a clock face
prompt: At 3:40, through how many degrees has the hour hand of a clock turned clockwise from the 12 on the clock face?
explanation: The hour hand moves 30° per hour and keeps moving during the hour, 0.5° per minute, so at 3:40 it has turned 3 x 30 + 40 x 0.5 = 110 degrees. "90" is 3 x 30, the hour hand parked on the 3 as though it did not drift. "120" is 4 x 30, reading the hand as already at the 4. "130" is the angle BETWEEN the two hands at 3:40, |110 - 240|, not the hour hand’s turn from the 12.

subskill: midsegment of a triangle
prompt: In the figure below, D is the midpoint of side AB of triangle ABC and E is the midpoint of side AC. All lengths are in centimeters. What is the length of BC, in centimeters?

explanation: A segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is half as long as the third side, so BC is twice DE: 2 x 11 = 22 centimeters. "11" takes DE and BC to be congruent. "5.5" halves DE instead of doubling it. "14" is twice AD, which gives the length of AB, a different side of the triangle.

subskill: the effect on a cylinder’s volume of scaling its dimensions
prompt: A cylindrical can holds 1,200 cubic centimeters. A second cylindrical can has a radius 50% greater than the first can’s and a height 20% less than the first can’s. How many cubic centimeters does the second can hold?
explanation: Volume is πr^2h, so the radius factor enters squared: the new volume is 1,200 x 1.5^2 x 0.8 = 1,200 x 1.8 = 2,160 cubic centimeters. "1440" scales the radius only once, 1,200 x 1.5 x 0.8. "2700" squares the radius factor but forgets the shorter height, 1,200 x 2.25. "1560" adds the percent changes, 1,200 x 1.3, instead of multiplying the factors.

subskill: distance from a point to a line in the coordinate plane
prompt: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, what is the distance from the point (7, 2) to the line 3x + 4y = 10, to the nearest tenth?
explanation: The distance from a point to a line is |3(7) + 4(2) - 10| divided by the square root of 3^2 + 4^2, which is 19/5 = 3.8. "4.8" measures straight down instead of perpendicular: the line passes through (7, −2.75), and 2 - (−2.75) = 4.75. "4.2" is the distance to the point where the line crosses the x-axis, (10/3, 0), which is not the closest point on the line. "7.2" divides 19 by the square root of 3 + 4 rather than the square root of 3^2 + 4^2.

subskill: a right triangle inscribed in a circle on a diameter
prompt: In the figure below, AB is a diameter of the circle, point C lies on the circle, and O is the centre. All lengths are in centimeters. What is the radius of the circle, in centimeters?

graphic.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 350 250" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#12151C"><circle cx="175" cy="130" r="95" fill="none" stroke="#2B3A8C" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="80" y1="130" x2="270" y2="130" stroke="#0A5C48" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="80" y1="130" x2="122" y2="51" stroke="#0A5C48" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="122" y1="51" x2="270" y2="130" stroke="#0A5C48" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="175" cy="130" r="3.2" fill="#12151C"/><text x="62" y="136">A</text><text x="274" y="136">B</text><text x="114" y="44">C</text><text x="170" y="148">O</text><text x="64" y="94">16</text><text x="203" y="80">30</text><text x="16" y="240" font-size="11" fill="#5A6474">Figure not drawn to scale.</text></svg>
graphic.caption: Figure not drawn to scale.

explanation: An angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle, so angle ACB is right and AB is the hypotenuse: AB is the square root of 16^2 + 30^2 = 1,156, which is 34, and the radius is half of that, 17 centimeters. "34" is the diameter, one halving short of the radius. "23" averages the two given sides, (16 + 30)/2, instead of using the Pythagorean theorem. "21.9" is the square root of 16 x 30, the geometric mean of the sides, which describes the altitude to the hypotenuse rather than any radius.

subskill: surface area of a sphere from its volume
prompt: A sphere has a volume of 288π cubic inches. What is the surface area of the sphere, in square inches?
explanation: From (4/3)πr^3 = 288π we get r^3 = 216 and r = 6, so the surface area is 4πr^2 = 4π(36) = 144π square inches. "288π" repeats the given volume. "36π" is πr^2, the area of a great circle of the sphere, a quarter of the true surface area. "576π" puts the diameter 12 into 4πr^2 in place of the radius.

subskill: painted unit cubes cut from a larger cube
prompt: A wooden cube 5 centimeters on each edge is painted on all six of its faces and then cut into 1-centimeter cubes. How many of the small cubes have paint on exactly two faces?
explanation: Exactly two painted faces means a cube on an edge but not at a corner. Each of the 12 edges contributes 5 - 2 = 3 such cubes, so there are 12 x 3 = 36. "44" adds the 8 corner cubes, 36 + 8, which counts the cubes with AT LEAST two painted faces. "54" is 6 x 3^2, the cubes with exactly ONE painted face, the interiors of the six faces. "60" is 12 x 5, every cube lying along an edge, which double-counts the corners and includes them.
